study.title: Make haste, O God, to deliver me!
study.intro: Five urgent verses ask God to hurry: shame the mockers, gladden all who seek Him, and come quickly to a poor and needy servant.
study.context: The heading names the choirmaster and David and adds 'To bring remembrance', also found on Psalm 38, perhaps linked to a memorial offering or simply to asking God to remember. Psalm 70 is nearly identical to Psalm 40:13–17, with small changes, such as 'God' in place of 'LORD' in places. It seems the closing prayer of Psalm 40 was lifted out to stand as a short prayer for times of emergency. It opens and closes with the plea for haste, framing prayers about enemies and about the joy of those who seek God.
study.peopleNote: The heading names David. David's profile gives background on the dangers and enemies that shaped many of his prayers. Planned paintings show roads, hills and anonymous people; God is never portrayed as a human body.

verses.title: Make haste
verses.heading: An emergency prayer
verses.meaning: The psalm begins at full speed: 'Make haste, O God, to deliver me! Hurry, O LORD, to help me!' There are no long titles or explanations, just a double cry for speed. The heading 'To bring remembrance' may suggest asking God to remember His servant. This is the kind of prayer people pray in the car, the hospital hallway or the middle of the night. Psalm 70 shows that short, urgent prayers are real prayers and belong in Scripture's songbook.
verses.context: Psalm 40:13 reads, 'Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; hurry, O LORD, to help me.' Psalm 38:22 also ends, 'Hurry to help me, O Lord my Savior.' Peter's 'Lord, save me!' in Matthew 14:30 is the same kind of brief cry.
explore: To bring remembrance
A heading also on Psalm 38. It may relate to a memorial offering or to asking God to remember.
Make haste
Hurry. The plea asks God to act without delay because the danger is immediate.
verses.reflect: What short prayer could you keep ready for moments of sudden need?
verses.alt: A villager in a head cloth runs along a dusty road toward a hilltop in early light.

verses.title: Turned back
verses.heading: Shame for those who seek harm
verses.meaning: David prays that those seeking his life would be 'ashamed and confounded', and that those wishing him harm would be 'repelled and humiliated.' He is not asking for the power to strike back; he is asking God to make their plans fail and turn them back. In a culture of honor, shame meant the collapse of someone's schemes in public view. The prayer hands enemies to God and asks that evil not succeed.
verses.context: Psalm 35:4 asks that those who seek David's life be disgraced and turned back. Psalm 40:14 contains nearly the same words. Esther 7:10 tells how Haman was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.
explore: Confounded
Confused and thrown into disorder, so that plans fall apart.
Repelled
Driven back or turned away, like an attacking force forced to retreat.
verses.reflect: How might praying for evil plans to fail be different from wishing harm on people?
verses.alt: A band of armed men turns back down a narrow mountain pass under a darkening sky.

verses.title: Aha, aha!
verses.heading: Silencing mockers
verses.meaning: Verse 3 names a specific kind of enemy: those who say 'Aha, aha!' This is the sound of gloating, the jeer of people who enjoy another's fall. David asks that they 'retreat because of their shame.' Their mocking laughter will turn to embarrassment when God acts. Scripture often notes that God sees gloating over others' misfortune, and Proverbs warns not to rejoice when an enemy falls. God takes the side of those who are laughed at.
verses.context: Psalm 35:21 says enemies opened their mouths and said, 'Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it!' Ezekiel 25:3 condemns Ammon for saying 'Aha!' over Israel's ruin. Proverbs 24:17 warns, 'Do not gloat when your enemy falls.'
explore: Aha, aha
A taunting shout of triumph, the sound of someone enjoying another's trouble.
Retreat
To pull back or withdraw, here in embarrassment as the gloating turns to shame.
verses.reflect: Have you ever felt tempted to gloat when someone else failed, and how can you resist it?
verses.alt: Jeering figures on a wall fall silent and step back as dawn light spreads over the town.

verses.title: Let God be magnified
verses.heading: Joy for all who seek Him
verses.meaning: In the center the psalm widens its view. David prays for everyone who seeks God, that they would 'rejoice and be glad in You.' Those who love His salvation will keep saying, 'Let God be magnified!' To magnify God is not to make Him bigger but to make Him look as great as He is, like a magnifying glass helps us see clearly. Even in an emergency David remembers that his rescue is part of something larger: God's people rejoicing in Him.
verses.context: Psalm 34:3 says, 'Magnify the LORD with me; let us exalt His name together.' Mary begins her song in Luke 1:46, 'My soul magnifies the Lord.' Psalm 40:16 has nearly identical words.
explore: Magnified
Declared great, so that others see God's greatness more clearly.
Love Your salvation
To treasure God's rescue and delight in His saving work, not just receive it.
verses.reflect: What could you say today that would help someone else see how great God is?
verses.alt: Families gather on a hillside at sunrise, arms raised and faces turned toward the light.

verses.title: Poor and needy
verses.heading: Do not delay
verses.meaning: David ends by turning back to himself: 'But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God.' He makes no claim to strength or worthiness, only need. Then he states his confidence: 'You are my help and my deliverer.' The psalm does not end with the answer but with the plea, 'O LORD, do not delay.' Faith sometimes ends a prayer still waiting. Yet calling God 'my help' shows David already knows where help will come from.
verses.context: Psalm 40:17 says, 'I am poor and needy; may the Lord think of me.' Psalm 121:2 says, 'My help comes from the LORD.' Matthew 5:3 calls blessed those who are poor in spirit.
explore: Poor and needy
Lacking resources and strength, a humble admission of total dependence on God.
Deliverer
One who rescues and sets free. David names God as the One who will save him.
verses.reflect: How can you admit your need to God today while still trusting that He is your help?
verses.alt: A person sits by a well at midday, looking up the road with patient hope.
